04.ad47eb6a26:
<n>45:2</n> Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adjútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
<n>45:3</n> Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
<n>45:4</n> Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine ejus.
<n>45:5</n> Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
<n>45:6</n> Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur: * adjuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
<n>45:7</n> Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
<n>45:8</n> Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
<n>45:9</n> Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.
<n>45:10</n> Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.
<n>45:11</n> Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
<n>45:12</n> Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
04.8045a3d532:
<n>45:2</n> Our God is our refuge and strength: * a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.
<n>45:3</n> Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; * and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.
<n>45:4</n> Their waters roared and were troubled: * the mountains were troubled with his strength.
<n>45:5</n> The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: * the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.
<n>45:6</n> God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: * God will help it in the morning early.
<n>45:7</n> Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: * he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.
<n>45:8</n> The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.
<n>45:9</n> Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth, * making wars to cease even to the end of the earth.
<n>45:10</n> He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: * and the shield he shall burn in the fire.
<n>45:11</n> Be still and see that I am God; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.
<n>45:12</n> The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.
04.8332aa2c37:
<n>44:2</n> Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
<n>44:2</n> Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
<n>44:3</n> Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
<n>44:4</n> Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
<n>44:5</n> Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
<n>44:5</n> Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et justítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
<n>44:6</n> Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
<n>44:7</n> Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
<n>44:8</n> Dilexísti justítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
<n>44:9</n> Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
<n>44:10</n> Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
<n>44:11</n> Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
<n>44:12</n> Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
<n>44:13</n> Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
<n>44:14</n> Omnis glória ejus fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
<n>44:15</n> Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi.
<n>44:16</n> Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
<n>44:17</n> Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
<n>44:18</n> Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
<n>44:18</n> Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
04.07e2806e17:
<n>44:2</n> My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.
<n>44:2</n> My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.
<n>44:3</n> Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.
<n>44:4</n> Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.
<n>44:5</n> With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.
<n>44:5</n> Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.
<n>44:6</n> Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.
<n>44:7</n> Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.
<n>44:8</n> Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.
<n>44:9</n> Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.
<n>44:10</n> The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.
<n>44:11</n> Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.
<n>44:12</n> And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.
<n>44:13</n> And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.
<n>44:14</n> All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.
<n>44:15</n> After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.
<n>44:16</n> They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.
<n>44:17</n> Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.
<n>44:18</n> They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.
<n>44:18</n> Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.
04.d2dac55244:
<n>40:2</n> Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
<n>40:3</n> Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum ejus.
<n>40:4</n> Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris ejus: * univérsum stratum ejus versásti in infirmitáte ejus.
<n>40:5</n> Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
<n>40:6</n> Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen ejus?
<n>40:7</n> Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor ejus congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
<n>40:7</n> Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
<n>40:8</n> Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
<n>40:9</n> Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
<n>40:10</n> Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
<n>40:11</n> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
<n>40:12</n> In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
<n>40:13</n> Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
<n>40:14</n> Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
04.c6014b2b43:
<n>40:2</n> Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.
<n>40:3</n> The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.
<n>40:4</n> The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.
<n>40:5</n> I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.
<n>40:6</n> My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?
<n>40:7</n> And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.
<n>40:7</n> He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.
<n>40:8</n> All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.
<n>40:9</n> They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?
<n>40:10</n> For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.
<n>40:11</n> But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.
<n>40:12</n> By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.
<n>40:13</n> But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.
<n>40:14</n> Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.
04.84f9c99f34:
<n>41:2</n> Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
<n>41:3</n> Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
<n>41:4</n> Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
<n>41:5</n> Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
<n>41:5</n> In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
<n>41:6</n> Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
<n>41:6</n> Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
<n>41:7</n> Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Jordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
<n>41:8</n> Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.
<n>41:8</n> Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.
<n>41:9</n> In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum ejus.
<n>41:9</n> Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
<n>41:10</n> Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
<n>41:11</n> Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
<n>41:11</n> Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
<n>41:12</n> Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
04.fd48846c8b:
<n>41:2</n> As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.
<n>41:3</n> My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?
<n>41:4</n> My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?
<n>41:5</n> These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:
<n>41:5</n> With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.
<n>41:6</n> Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?
<n>41:6</n> Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.
<n>41:7</n> My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.
<n>41:8</n> Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.
<n>41:8</n> All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.
<n>41:9</n> In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.
<n>41:9</n> With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.
<n>41:10</n> Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?
<n>41:11</n> Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;
<n>41:11</n> Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?
<n>41:12</n> Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.
04.1c03cadd4c:
<n>42:1</n> Júdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam de gente non sancta, * ab hómine iníquo, et dolóso érue me.
<n>42:2</n> Quia tu es, Deus, fortitúdo mea: * quare me repulísti? et quare tristis incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
<n>42:3</n> Emítte lucem tuam et veritátem tuam: * ipsa me deduxérunt, et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum, et in tabernácula tua.
<n>42:4</n> Et introíbo ad altáre Dei: * ad Deum, qui lætíficat juventútem meam.
<n>42:5</n> Confitébor tibi in cíthara, Deus, Deus meus: * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
<n>42:6</n> Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
04.47ef19a6ca:
<n>42:1</n> Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation that is not holy: * deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.
<n>42:2</n> For thou art God my strength: * why hast thou cast me off? and why do I go sorrowful whilst the enemy afflicteth me?
<n>42:3</n> Send forth thy light and thy truth: * they have conducted me, and brought me unto thy holy hill, and into thy tabernacles.
<n>42:4</n> And I will go in to the altar of God: * to God who giveth joy to my youth.
<n>42:5</n> To thee, O God my God, I will give praise upon the harp: * why art thou sad, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?
<n>42:6</n> Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

04.2c28597fc6:
<n>43:2</n> Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
<n>43:2</n> Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.
<n>43:3</n> Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
<n>43:4</n> Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:
<n>43:4</n> Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.
<n>43:5</n> Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Jacob.
<n>43:6</n> In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
<n>43:7</n> Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.
<n>43:8</n> Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.
<n>43:9</n> In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
04.af3e654fd9:
<n>43:2</n> We have heard, O God, with our ears: * our fathers have declared to us,
<n>43:2</n> The work thou hast wrought in their days, * and in the days of old.
<n>43:3</n> Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: * thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.
<n>43:4</n> For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: * neither did their own arm save them.
<n>43:4</n> But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: * because thou wast pleased with them.
<n>43:5</n> Thou art thyself my king and my God, * who commandest the saving of Jacob.
<n>43:6</n> Through thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: * and through thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.
<n>43:7</n> For I will not trust in my bow: * neither shall my sword save me.
<n>43:8</n> But thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: * and hast put them to shame that hate us.
<n>43:9</n> In God shall we glory all the day long: * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.
04.8421991721:
<n>43:10</n> Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
<n>43:11</n> Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.
<n>43:12</n> Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
<n>43:13</n> Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
<n>43:14</n> Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
<n>43:15</n> Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.
<n>43:16</n> Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
<n>43:17</n> A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.
<n>43:18</n> Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
<n>43:19</n> Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:
<n>43:20</n> Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
04.9c4d25945f:
<n>43:10</n> But now thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: * and thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.
<n>43:11</n> Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: * and they that hated us plundered for themselves.
<n>43:12</n> Thou hast given us up like sheep to be eaten: * thou hast scattered us among the nations.
<n>43:13</n> Thou hast sold thy people for no price: * and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.
<n>43:14</n> Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, * a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.
<n>43:15</n> Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: * a shaking of the head among the people.
<n>43:16</n> All the day long my shame is before me: * and the confusion of my face hath covered me.
<n>43:17</n> At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: * at the face of the enemy and persecutor.
<n>43:18</n> All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten thee: * and we have not done wickedly in thy covenant.
<n>43:19</n> And our heart hath not turned back: * neither hast thou turned aside our steps from thy way.
<n>43:20</n> For thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: * and the shadow of death hath covered us.
04.cea8012bc4:
<n>43:21</n> Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, * et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:
<n>43:22</n> Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.
<n>43:22</n> Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
<n>43:23</n> Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
<n>43:24</n> Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?
<n>43:25</n> Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
<n>43:26</n> Exsúrge, Dómine, ádjuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.
04.893e7fa8bc:
<n>43:21</n> If we have forgotten the name of our God, * and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:
<n>43:22</n> Shall not God search out these things: * for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.
<n>43:22</n> Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long: * we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.
<n>43:23</n> Arise, why sleepest thou, O Lord? * arise, and cast us not off to the end.
<n>43:24</n> Why turnest thou thy face away? * and forgettest our want and our trouble?
<n>43:25</n> For our soul is humbled down to the dust: * our belly cleaveth to the earth.
<n>43:26</n> Arise, O Lord, help us * and redeem us for thy name’s sake.
04.0279ba4b6a:
<n>44:2</n> Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
<n>44:2</n> Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
<n>44:3</n> Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
<n>44:4</n> Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
<n>44:5</n> Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
<n>44:5</n> Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et justítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
<n>44:6</n> Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
<n>44:7</n> Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
<n>44:8</n> Dilexísti justítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
<n>44:9</n> Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
<n>44:10</n> Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
04.74bbb203d6:
<n>44:2</n> My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.
<n>44:2</n> My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.
<n>44:3</n> Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.
<n>44:4</n> Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.
<n>44:5</n> With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.
<n>44:5</n> Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.
<n>44:6</n> Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.
<n>44:7</n> Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.
<n>44:8</n> Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.
<n>44:9</n> Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.
<n>44:10</n> The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.
04.46b17cc520:
<n>44:11</n> Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
<n>44:12</n> Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
<n>44:13</n> Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
<n>44:14</n> Omnis glória ejus fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
<n>44:15</n> Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi.
<n>44:16</n> Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
<n>44:17</n> Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
<n>44:18</n> Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
<n>44:18</n> Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
04.d4db90a7e6:
<n>44:11</n> Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.
<n>44:12</n> And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.
<n>44:13</n> And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.
<n>44:14</n> All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.
<n>44:15</n> After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.
<n>44:16</n> They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.
<n>44:17</n> Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.
<n>44:18</n> They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.
<n>44:18</n> Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.
04.c9591057d5:
<n>47:2</n> Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis * in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto ejus.
<n>47:3</n> Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
<n>47:4</n> Deus in dómibus ejus cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.
<n>47:5</n> Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.
<n>47:6</n> Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.
<n>47:7</n> Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
<n>47:9</n> Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
<n>47:10</n> Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.
<n>47:11</n> Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * justítia plena est déxtera tua.
<n>47:12</n> Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Judæ: * propter judícia tua, Dómine.
<n>47:13</n> Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus ejus.
<n>47:14</n> Pónite corda vestra in virtúte ejus: * et distribúite domos ejus, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.
<n>47:15</n> Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi: * ipse reget nos in sǽcula.
04.1790398483:
<n>47:2</n> Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised * in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.
<n>47:3</n> With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, * on the sides of the north, the city of the great king.
<n>47:4</n> In her houses shall God be known, * when he shall protect her.
<n>47:5</n> For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: * they gathered together.
<n>47:6</n> So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: * trembling took hold of them.
<n>47:7</n> There were pains as of a woman in labour; * with a vehement wind thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.
<n>47:9</n> As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: * God hath founded it for ever.
<n>47:10</n> We have received thy mercy, O God, * in the midst of thy temple.
<n>47:11</n> According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: * thy right hand is full of justice.
<n>47:12</n> Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad; * because of thy judgments, O Lord.
<n>47:13</n> Surround Sion, and encompass her: * tell ye in her towers.
<n>47:14</n> Set your hearts on her strength; and distribute her houses, * that ye may relate it in another generation.
<n>47:15</n> For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: * he shall rule us for evermore.
04.e6ef814cfc:
<n>48:2</n> Audíte hæc, omnes gentes: * áuribus percípite omnes, qui habitátis orbem:
<n>48:3</n> Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum: * simul in unum dives et pauper.
<n>48:4</n> Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam: * et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
<n>48:5</n> Inclinábo in parábolam aurem meam: * apériam in psaltério propositiónem meam.
<n>48:6</n> Cur timébo in die mala? * iníquitas calcánei mei circúmdabit me:
<n>48:7</n> Qui confídunt in virtúte sua: * et in multitúdine divitiárum suárum gloriántur.
<n>48:8</n> Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo: * non dabit Deo placatiónem suam.
<n>48:9</n> Et prétium redemptiónis ánimæ suæ: * et laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem.
<n>48:11</n> Non vidébit intéritum, cum víderit sapiéntes moriéntes: * simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt.
<n>48:11</n> Et relínquent aliénis divítias suas: * et sepúlcra eórum domus illórum in ætérnum.
<n>48:12</n> Tabernácula eórum in progénie et progénie: * vocavérunt nómina sua in terris suis.
<n>48:13</n> Et homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
04.546800b992:
<n>48:2</n> Hear these things, all ye nations: * give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world.
<n>48:3</n> All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men: * both rich and poor together.
<n>48:4</n> My mouth shall speak wisdom: * and the meditation of my heart understanding.
<n>48:5</n> I will incline my ear to a parable; * I will open my proposition on the psaltery.
<n>48:6</n> Why shall I fear in the evil day? * the iniquity of my heel shall encompass me.
<n>48:7</n> They that trust in their own strength, * and glory in the multitude of their riches,
<n>48:8</n> No brother can redeem, nor shall man redeem: * he shall not give to God his ransom,
<n>48:9</n> Nor the price of the redemption of his soul: * and shall labour for ever, and shall still live unto the end.
<n>48:11</n> He shall not see destruction, when he shall see the wise dying: * the senseless and the fool shall perish together:
<n>48:11</n> And they shall leave their riches to strangers: * and their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever.
<n>48:12</n> Their dwelling places to all generations: * they have called their lands by their names.
<n>48:13</n> And man when he was in honour did not understand; * he is compared to senseless beasts, and is become like to them.
04.5a683d134d:
<n>48:14</n> Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis: * et póstea in ore suo complacébunt.
<n>48:15</n> Sicut oves in inférno pósiti sunt: * mors depáscet eos.
<n>48:15</n> Et dominabúntur eórum justi in matutíno: * et auxílium eórum veteráscet in inférno a glória eórum.
<n>48:16</n> Verúmtamen Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi: * cum accéperit me.
<n>48:17</n> Ne timúeris, cum dives factus fúerit homo: * et cum multiplicáta fúerit glória domus ejus.
<n>48:18</n> Quóniam cum interíerit, non sumet ómnia: * neque descéndet cum eo glória ejus.
<n>48:19</n> Quia ánima ejus in vita ipsíus benedicétur: * confitébitur tibi cum beneféceris ei.
<n>48:20</n> Introíbit usque in progénies patrum suórum: * et usque in ætérnum non vidébit lumen.
<n>48:21</n> Homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
04.220194ad56:
<n>48:14</n> This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them: * and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth.
<n>48:15</n> They are laid in hell like sheep: * death shall feed upon them.
<n>48:15</n> And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning; * and their help shall decay in hell from their glory.
<n>48:16</n> But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, * when he shall receive me.
<n>48:17</n> Be not thou afraid, when a man shall be made rich, * and when the glory of his house shall be increased.
<n>48:18</n> For when he shall die he shall take nothing away; * nor shall his glory descend with him.
<n>48:19</n> For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed: * and he will praise thee when thou shalt do well to him.
<n>48:20</n> He shall go in to the generations of his fathers: * and he shall never see light.
<n>48:21</n> Man when he was in honour did not understand: * he hath been compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them.
04.648f8367d6:
<n>49:1</n> Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est: * et vocávit terram,
<n>49:1</n> A solis ortu usque ad occásum: * ex Sion spécies decóris ejus.
<n>49:3</n> Deus maniféste véniet: * Deus noster et non silébit.
<n>49:3</n> Ignis in conspéctu ejus exardéscet: * et in circúitu ejus tempéstas válida.
<n>49:4</n> Advocábit cælum desúrsum: * et terram discérnere pópulum suum.
<n>49:5</n> Congregáte illi sanctos ejus: * qui órdinant testaméntum ejus super sacrifícia.
<n>49:6</n> Et annuntiábunt cæli justítiam ejus: * quóniam Deus judex est.
<n>49:7</n> Audi, pópulus meus, et loquar: Israël, et testificábor tibi: * Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.
<n>49:8</n> Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te: * holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper.
<n>49:9</n> Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos: * neque de grégibus tuis hircos.
<n>49:10</n> Quóniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvárum: * juménta in móntibus et boves.
<n>49:11</n> Cognóvi ómnia volatília cæli: * et pulchritúdo agri mecum est.
<n>49:12</n> Si esuríero, non dicam tibi: * meus est enim orbis terræ, et plenitúdo ejus.
<n>49:13</n> Numquid manducábo carnes taurórum? * aut sánguinem hircórum potábo?
<n>49:14</n> Ímmola Deo sacrifícium laudis: * et redde Altíssimo vota tua.
<n>49:15</n> Et ínvoca me in die tribulatiónis: * éruam te, et honorificábis me.
04.e9ed765131:
<n>49:1</n> The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken: * and he hath called the earth.
<n>49:1</n> From the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof: * out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty.
<n>49:3</n> God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, * and shall not keep silence.
<n>49:3</n> A fire shall burn before him: * and a mighty tempest shall be round about.
<n>49:4</n> He shall call heaven from above, * and the earth, to judge his people.
<n>49:5</n> Gather ye together his saints to him: * who set his covenant before sacrifices.
<n>49:6</n> And the heavens shall declare his justice: * for God is judge.
<n>49:7</n> Hear, O my people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to thee: * I am God, thy God.
<n>49:8</n> I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices: * and thy burnt offerings are always in my sight.
<n>49:9</n> I will not take calves out of thy house: * nor he goats out of thy flocks.
<n>49:10</n> For all the beasts of the woods are mine: * the cattle on the hills, and the oxen.
<n>49:11</n> I know all the fowls of the air: * and with me is the beauty of the field.
<n>49:12</n> If I should be hungry, I would not tell thee: * for the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.
<n>49:13</n> Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? * or shall I drink the blood of goats?
<n>49:14</n> Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: * and pay thy vows to the most High.
<n>49:15</n> And call upon me in the day of trouble: * I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.
04.d7633a2c1b:
<n>49:16</n> Peccatóri autem dixit Deus: * Quare tu enárras justítias meas, et assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum?
<n>49:17</n> Tu vero odísti disciplínam: * et projecísti sermónes meos retrórsum:
<n>49:18</n> Si vidébas furem, currébas cum eo: * et cum adúlteris portiónem tuam ponébas.
<n>49:19</n> Os tuum abundávit malítia: * et lingua tua concinnábat dolos.
<n>49:20</n> Sedens advérsus fratrem tuum loquebáris, et advérsus fílium matris tuæ ponébas scándalum: * hæc fecísti, et tácui.
<n>49:21</n> Existimásti, iníque, quod ero tui símilis: * árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam.
<n>49:22</n> Intellégite hæc, qui obliviscímini Deum: * nequándo rápiat, et non sit qui erípiat.
<n>49:23</n> Sacrifícium laudis honorificábit me: * et illic iter, quo osténdam illi salutáre Dei.
04.9484082c06:
<n>49:16</n> But to the sinner God hath said: * Why dost thou declare my justices, and take my covenant in thy mouth?
<n>49:17</n> Seeing thou hast hated discipline: * and hast cast my words behind thee.
<n>49:18</n> If thou didst see a thief thou didst run with him: * and with adulterers thou hast been a partaker.
<n>49:19</n> Thy mouth hath abounded with evil, * and thy tongue framed deceits.
<n>49:20</n> Sitting thou didst speak against thy brother, and didst lay a scandal against thy mother’s son: * these things hast thou done, and I was silent.
<n>49:21</n> Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: * but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face.
<n>49:22</n> Understand these things, you that forget God; * lest he snatch you away, and there be none to deliver you.
<n>49:23</n> The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me: * and there is the way by which I will shew him the salvation of God.
04.b9962dc5b5:
<n>45:15</n> Vere tu es Deus abscónditus, * Deus Israël, Salvátor.
<n>45:16</n> Confúsi sunt, et erubuérunt omnes: * simul abiérunt in confusiónem fabricatóres errórum.
<n>45:17</n> Israël salvátus est in Dómino salúte ætérna: * non confundémini, et non erubescétis usque in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>45:18</n> Quia hæc dicit Dóminus creans cælos, * ipse Deus formans terram, et fáciens eam, ipse plastes ejus:
<n>45:19</n> Non in vanum creávit eam, ut habitarétur, formávit eam: * Ego Dóminus, et non est álius.
<n>45:20</n> Non in abscóndito locútus sum, * in loco terræ tenebróso:
<n>45:21</n> Non dixi sémini Jacob frustra: Quǽrite me: * ego Dóminus loquens justítiam, annúntians recta.
<n>45:22</n> Congregámini, et veníte, et accédite simul * qui salváti estis ex géntibus:
<n>45:23</n> Nesciérunt qui levant lignum sculptúræ suæ, * et rogant deum non salvántem.
<n>45:24</n> Annuntiáte, et veníte, et consiliámini simul: * Quis audítum fecit hoc ab inítio, ex tunc prædíxit illud?
<n>45:25</n> Numquid non ego Dóminus, et non est ultra Deus absque me? * Deus justus, et salvans non est præter me.
<n>45:26</n> Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis, omnes fines terræ: * quia ego Deus, et non est álius.
<n>45:27</n> In memetípso jurávi, egrediétur de ore meo justítiæ verbum, * et non revertétur:
<n>45:28</n> Quia mihi curvábitur omne genu, * et jurábit omnis lingua.
<n>45:29</n> Ergo in Dómino, dicet, meæ sunt justítiæ et impérium: * ad eum vénient, et confundéntur omnes qui repúgnant ei.
<n>45:30</n> In Dómino justificábitur, et laudábitur * omne semen Israël.
04.b8b8f62bd4:
<n>45:15</n> Verily thou art a hidden God, * the God of Israel the saviour.
<n>45:16</n> They are all confounded and ashamed: * the forgers of errors are gone together into confusion.
<n>45:17</n> Israel is saved in the Lord with an eternal salvation: * you shall not be confounded, and you shall not be ashamed for ever and ever.
<n>45:18</n> For thus saith the Lord that created the heavens, * God himself that formed the earth, and made it, the very maker thereof:
<n>45:19</n> He did not create it in vain: he formed it to be inhabited. * I am the Lord, and there is no other.
<n>45:20</n> I have not spoken in secret, * in a dark place of the earth:
<n>45:21</n> I have not said to the seed of Jacob: Seek me in vain. * I am the Lord that speak justice, that declare right things.
<n>45:22</n> Assemble yourselves, and come, and draw near together, * ye that are saved of the Gentiles:
<n>45:23</n> They have no knowledge that set up the wood of their graven work, * and pray to a god that cannot save.
<n>45:24</n> Tell ye, and come, and consult together: * who hath declared this from the beginning, who hath foretold this from that time?
<n>45:25</n> Have not I the Lord, and there is no God else besides me? * A just God and a saviour, there is none besides me.
<n>45:26</n> Be converted to me, and you shall be saved, all ye ends of the earth: * for I am God, and there is no other.
<n>45:27</n> I have sworn by myself, the word of justice shall go out of my mouth, * and shall not return:
<n>45:28</n> For every knee shall be bowed to me, * and every tongue shall swear.
<n>45:29</n> Therefore shall he say: In the Lord are my justices and empire: * they shall come to him, and all that resist him shall be confounded.
<n>45:30</n> In the Lord shall all the seed * of Israel be justified and praised.
04.971d51fbc5:
<n>46:2</n> Omnes gentes, pláudite mánibus: * jubiláte Deo in voce exsultatiónis.
<n>46:3</n> Quóniam Dóminus excélsus, terríbilis: * Rex magnus super omnem terram.
<n>46:4</n> Subjécit pópulos nobis: * et gentes sub pédibus nostris.
<n>46:5</n> Elégit nobis hereditátem suam: * spéciem Jacob, quam diléxit.
<n>46:6</n> Ascéndit Deus in júbilo: * et Dóminus in voce tubæ.
<n>46:7</n> Psállite Deo nostro, psállite: * psállite Regi nostro, psállite.
<n>46:8</n> Quóniam Rex omnis terræ Deus: * psállite sapiénter.
<n>46:9</n> Regnábit Deus super gentes: * Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam.
<n>46:10</n> Príncipes populórum congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham: * quóniam dii fortes terræ veheménter eleváti sunt.
04.75f48e9010:
<n>46:2</n> O clap your hands, all ye nations: * shout unto God with the voice of joy,
<n>46:3</n> For the Lord is high, terrible: * a great king over all the earth.
<n>46:4</n> He hath subdued the people under us; * and the nations under our feet.
<n>46:5</n> He hath chosen for us his inheritance, * the beauty of Jacob which he hath loved.
<n>46:6</n> God is ascended with jubilee, * and the Lord with the sound of trumpet.
<n>46:7</n> Sing praises to our God, sing ye: * sing praises to our king, sing ye.
<n>46:8</n> For God is the king of all the earth: * sing ye wisely.
<n>46:9</n> God shall reign over the nations: * God sitteth on his holy throne.
<n>46:10</n> The princes of the people are gathered together, with the God of Abraham: * for the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted.
04.9c4023b8dd:
<n>49:1</n> Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est: * et vocávit terram,
<n>49:1</n> A solis ortu usque ad occásum: * ex Sion spécies decóris ejus.
<n>49:3</n> Deus maniféste véniet: * Deus noster et non silébit.
<n>49:3</n> Ignis in conspéctu ejus exardéscet: * et in circúitu ejus tempéstas válida.
<n>49:4</n> Advocábit cælum desúrsum: * et terram discérnere pópulum suum.
<n>49:5</n> Congregáte illi sanctos ejus: * qui órdinant testaméntum ejus super sacrifícia.
<n>49:6</n> Et annuntiábunt cæli justítiam ejus: * quóniam Deus judex est.
04.7807c01cd5:
<n>49:1</n> The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken: * and he hath called the earth.
<n>49:1</n> From the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof: * out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty.
<n>49:3</n> God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, * and shall not keep silence.
<n>49:3</n> A fire shall burn before him: * and a mighty tempest shall be round about.
<n>49:4</n> He shall call heaven from above, * and the earth, to judge his people.
<n>49:5</n> Gather ye together his saints to him: * who set his covenant before sacrifices.
<n>49:6</n> And the heavens shall declare his justice: * for God is judge.
04.1080e5ef82:
<n>49:7</n> Audi, pópulus meus, et loquar: Israël, et testificábor tibi: * Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.
<n>49:8</n> Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te: * holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper.
<n>49:9</n> Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos: * neque de grégibus tuis hircos.
<n>49:10</n> Quóniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvárum: * juménta in móntibus et boves.
<n>49:11</n> Cognóvi ómnia volatília cæli: * et pulchritúdo agri mecum est.
<n>49:12</n> Si esuríero, non dicam tibi: * meus est enim orbis terræ, et plenitúdo ejus.
<n>49:13</n> Numquid manducábo carnes taurórum? * aut sánguinem hircórum potábo?
<n>49:14</n> Ímmola Deo sacrifícium laudis: * et redde Altíssimo vota tua.
<n>49:15</n> Et ínvoca me in die tribulatiónis: * éruam te, et honorificábis me.
04.4c957546ab:
<n>49:7</n> Hear, O my people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to thee: * I am God, thy God.
<n>49:8</n> I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices: * and thy burnt offerings are always in my sight.
<n>49:9</n> I will not take calves out of thy house: * nor he goats out of thy flocks.
<n>49:10</n> For all the beasts of the woods are mine: * the cattle on the hills, and the oxen.
<n>49:11</n> I know all the fowls of the air: * and with me is the beauty of the field.
<n>49:12</n> If I should be hungry, I would not tell thee: * for the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.
<n>49:13</n> Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? * or shall I drink the blood of goats?
<n>49:14</n> Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: * and pay thy vows to the most High.
<n>49:15</n> And call upon me in the day of trouble: * I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.
